questions.question: SBM Bank India entered into a bancassurance partnership with which among the following companies in May 2025?

options.text: Axis Max Life Insurance Co. Ltd.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ICICI Prudential Life Insurance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **SBM Bank India** entered into a strategic **bancassurance** partnership with **ICICI Prudential Life Insurance** to provide its customers with a comprehensive range of **life insurance** products.
 
• Through this partnership, **SBM Bank India** aims to offer its **private banking** and **retail** customers a diverse portfolio of insurance solutions, including **wealth management**, **retirement**, and **protection** plans.
 
• This collaboration leverages **SBM Bank's** extensive distribution network and **ICICI Prudential's** digital-first approach to provide seamless **financial services**.
 
• The primary objective of this tie-up is to enhance **financial security** and provide **long-term savings** options to the bank's growing client base across **India**.
 
• The agreement signifies a major step for **SBM Bank India** in becoming a one-stop destination for all **financial and insurance** needs of its customers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bancassurance**:
 
 
• It is an arrangement between a **bank** and an **insurance company** that allows the insurance company to sell its products to the bank's client base.
 
• This partnership benefits the bank through **commission-based income** and provides the insurance company with a wide **distribution channel**.
 
 
 
• **SBM Bank India**:
 
 
• It is the first bank in India to receive a **Universal Banking License** from the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** to operate as a **Wholly Owned Subsidiary (WOS)** of a foreign bank.
 
• The bank is headquartered in **Mumbai** and is a subsidiary of **SBM Holdings**, which is based in **Mauritius**.
 
• The bank focuses on **corporate banking**, **retail banking**, and **wealth management** with a strong emphasis on **technology-driven** solutions.
 
 
 
• **ICICI Prudential Life Insurance**:
 
 
• It is a joint venture between **ICICI Bank Limited** and **Prudential Corporation Holdings Limited**.
 
• The company began operations in **December 2000** and was the first **private sector** life insurance company to be listed on the **National Stock Exchange (NSE)** and **Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE)**.
 
• It offers a wide range of products including **Term Insurance**, **Health Insurance**, and **Unit Linked Insurance Plans (ULIPs)**.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Framework**:
 
 
• The **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** governs the guidelines for **bancassurance** to ensure that consumer interests are protected and **mis-selling** is prevented.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Financial Inclusion**: Such partnerships are vital for increasing **insurance penetration** in **India**, especially among the middle-class and affluent segments served by private banks.
 
• **Digital Integration**: Both entities emphasize **digital ecosystems**, allowing customers to purchase and manage policies via **mobile banking** and **internet banking** platforms.
 
• **SBM Bank's Presence**: As of **2024-2025**, the bank has been expanding its footprint in **metropolitan cities** and through **Neo-banking** partnerships to reach a wider demographic.
</ul

questions.question: What was the name of the bilateral Indo-French military drill held from 18 June to 1 July 2025 at Camp Larzac?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The bilateral military exercise named **Shakti 2025** was conducted between the **Indian Army** and the **French Army**.
 
• The exercise took place over a period of two weeks, starting from **18 June** and concluding on **1 July 2025**.
 
• The venue for this edition of the drill was **Camp Larzac**, which is a prominent military training facility located in **France**.
 
• The primary focus of **Exercise Shakti** is to enhance **interoperability** between the two armed forces and to share **combat experience** and **best practices** in the domain of **counter-terrorism** and **sub-conventional operations**.
 
• The drill involves high-intensity training, including **joint planning**, **tactical maneuvers**, and **neutralization of threat** scenarios, typically under a **United Nations** mandate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History and Frequency**: **Exercise Shakti** is a **biennial** training event that alternates between **India** and **France**. The **first edition** of this exercise was held in **2011**.
 
• **Indo-French Defense Cooperation**: India and France share a deep **Strategic Partnership** established in **1998**. Defense cooperation is one of the strongest pillars of this relationship, involving **technology transfer**, **joint production**, and regular **military dialogues**.
 
• **Other Bilateral Exercises**:
 
 
• **Exercise Varuna**: A bilateral **Naval** exercise that highlights the maritime cooperation between the **Indian Navy** and the **French Navy**.
 
• **Exercise Garuda**: A bilateral **Air Force** exercise involving the **Indian Air Force (IAF)** and the **French Air and Space Force**.
 
• **Exercise Desert Knight**: A complex air exercise often involving multi-national participation but rooted in Indo-French cooperation.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Camp Larzac**: Located in **Southern France**, **Camp Larzac** provides a diverse and challenging **geographical terrain** suitable for simulating various operational environments, making it an ideal location for **infantry-based** drills.
 
• **Equipment and Participation**: During these exercises, both nations often deploy their latest military hardware. The **Indian Army** typically sends a contingent from one of its **Infantry Regiments** (such as the **Rajput Regiment** or **Gorkha Rifles**) to participate alongside French counterparts.

• **Strategic Objectives**: The **Shakti 2025** exercise serves to strengthen the **diplomatic ties** between **New Delhi** and **Paris**, ensuring both nations can respond effectively to **global security challenges**.
 
• **Joint Operations**: Such exercises allow for the development of **Joint Command** structures, where officers from both countries work together to execute **mission-critical** tasks.
 
• **2024 Edition**: For context, the **7th edition** of **Exercise Shakti** was held in **May 2024** at the **Umroi Joint Training Node** in **Meghalaya, India**, showcasing the **alternating nature** of the hosting responsibilities.

questions.question: In November 2025, Narendra Modi presented a revolutionary indigenous innovation of India, as the country’s indigenous quantum security chip called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Quantum Security Integrated Processor (QSIP)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **November 2025**, Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** unveiled the **Quantum Security Integrated Processor (QSIP)**, marking a historic achievement in India's **indigenous** technological capabilities.
 
• The **QSIP** is India's first fully **locally designed and developed** quantum-secure semiconductor chip, aimed at protecting the nation's **digital sovereignty**.
 
• This innovation is a cornerstone of the **National Quantum Mission (NQM)**, which was initiated to position India as a global leader in **Quantum Technology (QT)**.
 
• The chip is specifically engineered to provide **hardware-level encryption** that is resistant to the immense processing power of future **quantum computers**, which threaten to break existing **RSA** and **ECC** encryption standards.
 
• The development of **QSIP** aligns with the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative, reducing India's reliance on foreign-made **cryptographic modules** and ensuring secure communication for **defense** and **government** sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Quantum Mission (NQM):**
 
 
• The **Union Cabinet** approved the **NQM** in **April 2023** with a total financial outlay of **₹6,003.65 crore** for the period **2023-24 to 2030-31**.
 
• The mission aims to develop intermediate-scale **quantum computers** with **50-1000 physical qubits** in various platforms like superconducting and photonic technology.
 
• It also focuses on **Quantum Communications**, specifically **Quantum Key Distribution (QKD)** over long distances, including satellite-based secure communications.
 
 
 
• **Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC):**
 
 
• **PQC** refers to mathematical **algorithms** that are thought to be secure against a cryptanalytic attack by a **quantum computer**.
 
• The **QSIP** chip integrates these **PQC** standards to ensure that data remains protected even as quantum computing power scales globally.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Applications:**
 
 
• The chip is designed for use in **critical infrastructure** such as **power grids**, **banking systems**, and **strategic defense networks**.
 
• It facilitates **Quantum Random Number Generation (QRNG)**, which provides a higher level of entropy compared to classical pseudo-random generators, making encryption keys nearly impossible to predict.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Semiconductor Mission connection:** The production of the **QSIP** chip is part of the broader **India Semiconductor Mission (ISM)**, which seeks to build a vibrant semiconductor and display ecosystem in the country.
 
• **Global Standing:** With the launch of **QSIP**, India joins an elite group of nations—including the **USA**, **China**, and **France**—that possess high-end **quantum-secure hardware** technology.
 
• **Cybersecurity Landscape:** As quantum computers can solve complex mathematical problems in seconds that would take classical computers **thousands of years**, the **QSIP** serves as a vital shield against "harvest now, decrypt later" strategies used by cyber-adversaries.
 
• **Collaborative Effort:** The design of the chip involved collaboration between the **Department of Science and Technology (DST)**, premier institutes like **IITs**, and **defense research laboratories**.

questions.question: In March 2025, which three Central Asian countries signed the Khujand Treaty to settle border disputes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Khujand Treaty** was officially signed in **March 2025** by the nations of **Tajikistan**, **Kyrgyzstan**, and **Uzbekistan** to settle long-standing territorial and border delimitation disputes.
 
• The treaty takes its name from **Khujand**, the second-largest city in **Tajikistan** and a major administrative center in the **Fergana Valley**, which served as the venue for the high-level diplomatic summit.
 
• The primary objective of the agreement is to finalize the demarcation of nearly **1,000 kilometers** of contested borders that have been a source of recurring conflict since the **dissolution of the Soviet Union** in **1991**.
 
• The signing involved the respective **Heads of State**, emphasizing a shift toward **Central Asian solidarity** and regional economic cooperation rather than military confrontation.
 
• The **Khujand Treaty** specifically addresses the management of **enclaves and exclaves**, ensuring that residents in these isolated territories have guaranteed transit rights and access to essential resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Fergana Valley:** 
 
 
• This region is shared by **Uzbekistan**, **Kyrgyzstan**, and **Tajikistan** and is the most densely populated area in **Central Asia**.
 
• Due to its **fertile soil** and strategic location, it has been the epicenter of ethnic tensions and border skirmishes over **land rights** and **irrigation water**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:** 
 
 
• The borders in this region were originally drawn during the **Stalinist era** of the **Soviet Union** without regard for ethnic distributions, leading to the creation of complex enclaves such as **Vorukh** (Tajik enclave in Kyrgyzstan) and **Sokh** (Uzbek enclave in Kyrgyzstan).
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Agreement:** 
 
 
• Settling these disputes is a prerequisite for major infrastructure projects, including the **China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan (CKU) railway**, which aims to enhance trade routes between **East Asia** and **Europe**.
 
• The **2025** treaty builds upon the momentum of the **2023** bilateral agreement between **Bishkek** and **Tashkent**, which successfully resolved their mutual border issues.
 
 
 
• **Regional Impact:** 
 
 
• By resolving these issues, the three countries aim to reduce the influence of external security actors and strengthen the role of the **Consultative Meetings of Central Asian Heads of State** as a primary forum for conflict resolution.
 
• It also minimizes the risk of **water-sharing conflicts**, which are expected to intensify in the **Amu Darya** and **Syr Darya** basins due to climate change.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Who among the following won the 2025 Abel Prize for contributions to algebraic analysis and representation theory?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Masaki Kashiwara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **2025 Abel Prize** has been awarded to the **Japanese mathematician Masaki Kashiwara** for his groundbreaking and transformative contributions to **algebraic analysis** and **representation theory**.
 
• **Masaki Kashiwara** is renowned for his work in creating the foundations of **microlocal analysis** alongside his mentor **Mikio Sato**, which allows for the study of **linear differential equations** using methods from **algebraic geometry** and **complex analysis**.
 
• He is credited with the development of **D-module theory**, a sophisticated mathematical framework that provides a deep connection between **analysis** and **algebra**, enabling researchers to solve complex problems in **theoretical physics** and **mathematics**.
 
• One of his most significant achievements in **representation theory** is the introduction of **crystal bases**. This concept revolutionized the study of **quantum groups** and their representations, providing a combinatorial way to understand these complex structures.
 
• The prize recognizes his lifetime of work at the **Research Institute for Mathematical Sciences (RIMS)** at **Kyoto University**, where he has influenced generations of mathematicians worldwide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Abel Prize:**
 
 
• It is an international award presented annually by the **Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters** to one or more outstanding mathematicians.
 
• Established by the **Government of Norway** in **2002**, it is named after the famous **Norwegian** mathematician **Niels Henrik Abel**, marking the **200th anniversary** of his birth.
 
• The prize is often referred to as the **"Nobel Prize of Mathematics"** because there is no Nobel category for the field of mathematics.
 
• The award ceremony traditionally takes place in **Oslo**, where the laureate receives a monetary prize of **7.5 million Norwegian kroner** (approximately **USD 700,000**).
 
 
 
• **Other Options Context:**
 
 
• **Terence Tao**: A world-renowned **Australian-American** mathematician and **Fields Medal** winner (**2006**), known for his work in **harmonic analysis** and **number theory**, but he is not the recipient of the 2025 Abel Prize.
 
• **Joel Mokyr** and **Philippe Aghion**: These are distinguished **economists** rather than pure mathematicians, specializing in **economic history** and **growth theory** respectively.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Algebraic Analysis:** This field, pioneered by the **Sato School** in **Japan**, treats **differential equations** as algebraic objects. This approach has led to major breakthroughs in **soliton theory** and **integrable systems**.
 
• **Global Recognition:** Before winning the **Abel Prize** in **2025**, **Masaki Kashiwara** received several other prestigious honors, including the **Kyoto Prize** in **Basic Sciences** (**2018**) and the **Chern Medal** (**2018**), which is awarded every four years at the **International Congress of Mathematicians (ICM)**.
 
• **Impact on Physics:** Kashiwara's theories, particularly in the realm of **representation theory** and **D-modules**, are extensively used in **string theory** and **conformal field theory**, bridging the gap between abstract **pure mathematics** and **theoretical physics**.
 
• **Selection Process:** The winner is selected by an international **Abel Committee** consisting of five leading mathematicians appointed by the **Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters**.
</ul

questions.question: During which of the following editions of the National Finite Element Developers’ meeting did Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) unveil the latest version of Finite Element Analysis of Structures (FEAST) software in February 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** unveiled the latest version of its indigenous structural analysis software, **FEAST (Finite Element Analysis of Structures)**, during the **8th edition** of the **National Finite Element Developers’ Meeting (NFEDM)**.
 
• The event was held in **February 2025** at the **Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC)** located in **Thiruvananthapuram**, Kerala.
 
• The **8th NFEDM** brought together experts, researchers, and developers from across the country to discuss advancements in **computational mechanics** and structural engineering.
 
• The release of the latest **FEAST** version is a significant milestone in India's pursuit of **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-reliant India) in the domain of sophisticated engineering software.
 
• The software is designed to provide a robust and cost-effective alternative to expensive foreign-made **Finite Element Analysis (FEA)** tools, reducing dependency on international licenses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About FEAST Software:**
 
 
• **FEAST** stands for **Finite Element Analysis of Structures**. It is a comprehensive software package developed by **VSSC/ISRO** for **linear** and **non-linear** structural analysis.
 
• It is used to analyze the structural integrity of **rockets**, **satellites**, and **launch vehicles**, ensuring they can withstand the extreme forces experienced during space missions.
 
• The software supports a wide range of applications, including **static**, **dynamic**, **thermal**, and **buckling** analysis of complex structures.
 
• It is available in various versions, such as **Academic** (for students), **Premium** (for small-scale industries), and **Professional** (for large enterprises).
 
 
 
• **National Finite Element Developers’ Meeting (NFEDM):**
 
 
• The **NFEDM** is a biennial or periodic national-level platform initiated to foster collaboration among **Indian developers** of structural analysis tools.
 
• It aims to create a unified ecosystem for **Finite Element Method (FEM)** development in India, encouraging the use of indigenous technologies in **aerospace**, **defense**, and **civil engineering**.
 
 
 
• **Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC):**
 
 
• Located in **Thiruvananthapuram**, **VSSC** is the lead center of **ISRO** responsible for the design and development of launch vehicle technology.
 
• It was named after **Dr. Vikram Sarabhai**, the father of the Indian space program, and has been instrumental in developing the **SLV-3**, **ASLV**, **PSLV**, **GSLV**, and **LVM3**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technological Significance:** The development of **FEAST** by **ISRO** scientists highlights India's capability to produce high-end **Computer-Aided Engineering (CAE)** software that meets global standards.
 
• **Date and Timeline:** The **8th NFEDM** took place in **February 2025**, marking several years of continuous evolution since the initial versions of the software were conceptualized.
 
• **Economic Impact:** By utilizing **indigenous software**, Indian industries and academic institutions can save millions in **foreign exchange** that would otherwise be spent on proprietary software like **ANSYS** or **NASTRAN**.
 
• **User Base:** Beyond **ISRO**, the software is being increasingly adopted by the **Indian Navy**, **defense labs (DRDO)**, and several **IITs** and **NITs** for research and development purposes.

• The athlete has been instrumental in redefining **American** distance running benchmarks. The time of **12:45.27** represents an elite performance in the **men's 5,000 m**, a distance that requires **12.5 laps** of a standard **400 m** outdoor track.

• His training base in **Flagstaff, Arizona**, which sits at an elevation of approximately **7,000 feet**, is widely credited for his exceptional cardiovascular endurance and ability to compete against the world's best **East African** runners.
 
• At the **2024 U.S. Olympic Team Trials** held in **Eugene, Oregon**, **Nico Young** demonstrated his elite status by qualifying for the **Paris 2024 Olympic Games** in both the **5,000 m** and **10,000 m** events.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Grant Fisher**: 
 
 
• Prior to recent surges in times, **Grant Fisher** held the **American outdoor record** for the **5,000 m** with a time of **12:46.96**, set in **September 2022** at the **Diamond League** final in **Zurich**.
 
• **Fisher** is a **Stanford University** alumnus and a **Tokyo 2020** Olympian who has consistently lowered the **U.S.** records across multiple distances.
 
 
 
• **Yared Nuguse**: 
 
 
• **Yared Nuguse** is primarily celebrated as a middle-distance specialist. He holds the **American record** in the **mile** with a time of **3:43.97** and the **3,000 m** indoors.
 
• He represents **On Athletics Club (OAC)** and is known for his tactical racing and powerful "kick" in the final **400 meters**.

• Modern advancements in footwear technology, often called "**super spikes**," and the use of **Wavelight** technology (pacing lights on the track) have contributed to significantly faster times in the **2020s**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Professional Transition**: **Nico Young**’s decision to turn **professional** in **June 2024** followed one of the most successful **collegiate** seasons in history, including multiple **NCAA Division I** titles.
 
• **Olympic Qualification**: The **United States** long-distance squad for the **Paris 2024** games is considered one of the strongest in history, with athletes like **Young** and **Fisher** both capable of challenging for podium spots.

questions.question: As per the survey conducted by the Yale Program on Climate Change Communication and CVoter from December 5, 2024, to February 18, 2025, what percentage of Indians reported experiencing severe air pollution in the past 12 months?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**52%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the survey report titled **"Climate Change in the Indian Mind, 2025"**, which was conducted by the **Yale Program on Climate Change Communication** in collaboration with **CVoter**, approximately **52%** of Indians reported experiencing **severe air pollution** in the past **12 months**.
 
• The comprehensive survey was conducted over a period spanning from **December 5, 2024**, to **February 18, 2025**, capturing public sentiment across various demographics in India.
 
• The data highlights that a majority of the population is now physically witnessing the detrimental effects of environmental degradation, particularly in urban and industrial corridors where **smog** and **particulate matter** levels often exceed safety limits.
 
• The survey indicates that personal experience with **climate-related hazards** is becoming a primary driver of public concern, with air pollution being one of the most visible and frequently cited issues.
 
• In addition to air quality, the report found that a significant portion of respondents also observed extreme weather events, including **heatwaves** and **erratic rainfall**, which further underscores the vulnerability of the Indian population to **global warming**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Yale Program on Climate Change Communication (YPCCC):**
 
 
• Based at **Yale University**, this program conducts scientific research on public climate change knowledge, attitudes, and policy support.
 
• Their work often utilizes the **"Global Warming's Six Americas"** framework to segment the public into groups like **Alarmed**, **Concerned**, and **Disengaged**.
 
 
 
• **CVoter (Centre for Voting Opinion & Trends in Election Research):**
 
 
• An international polling agency headquartered in **India**, **CVoter** provided the field data and survey methodology for the **2025** report.
 
• The survey involved a **nationally representative sample** of thousands of Indian adults to ensure the findings reflected the diversity of the country.
 
 
 
• **Climate Change Awareness in India:**
 
 
• The **2025** study revealed that roughly **82%** of Indians believe that **global warming** is happening, a significant increase from previous decades.
 
• About **73%** of respondents noted that they have observed changes in **local rainfall patterns** over the past **10 years**.
 
• There is strong public support in India for government-led **climate action** and a transition toward **renewable energy** sources like **solar** and **wind power**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Air Quality Index (AQI) Context:** India frequently tops global lists for the most polluted cities, with **PM2.5** levels often reaching "Hazardous" categories during the **winter months** due to **stubble burning**, **vehicular emissions**, and **industrial discharge**.
 
• **Health Impact:** Severe air pollution in India is linked to chronic respiratory diseases, cardiovascular issues, and an estimated **1.6 million** premature deaths annually.
 
• **Social Segmentation:** The report categorized a large segment of Indians (approximately **70%**) as either **"Alarmed"** or **"Concerned"** about climate change, indicating a high level of psychological readiness for environmental policy changes.
 
• **Economic Vulnerability:** As a developing nation with a large **agrarian economy**, India faces unique challenges as **air pollution** and **global warming** directly impact crop yields and labor productivity.

questions.question: Where was the Khelo India Winter Games 2025 second phase held?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gulmarg**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Khelo India Winter Games 2025** is the **fifth edition** of this national-level multisport event, designed to promote winter sports culture and identify athletic talent across India.
 
• The **second phase** of the **2025** games was hosted in **Gulmarg**, situated in the **Baramulla district** of **Jammu and Kashmir**. This region is world-renowned for its snow-covered slopes and high-altitude terrain.
 
• While the **first phase** of the event took place in **Leh, Ladakh**, focusing on ice-based sports like **Ice Hockey** and **Ice Skating**, the **Gulmarg** phase was dedicated to snow-based disciplines.
 
• The event is organized by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** in collaboration with the **Sports Authority of India (SAI)** and the **Jammu & Kashmir Sports Council**.
 
• Key sports held during the **Gulmarg** phase included **Alpine Skiing**, **Nordic Skiing**, and **Snowboarding**, utilizing the specialized infrastructure of the **Gulmarg Gondola** and surrounding ridges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History of Khelo India Winter Games:** The inaugural edition of the **Winter Games** was held in **2020**. Since then, **Gulmarg** and **Leh** have remained the primary venues due to their unique geographical advantages.
 
• **Significance of Gulmarg:** Known as the "Heartland of Winter Sports in India," **Gulmarg** sits at an elevation of approximately **2,650 meters**. It features the **Gulmarg Gondola**, which is one of the highest cable cars in the world, facilitating international-standard skiing competitions.
 
• **Objectives:** The primary goal of the **Khelo India** initiative is to strengthen the sports ecosystem at the grassroots level and prepare Indian athletes for international competitions like the **Winter Olympics**.
 
• **Economic and Tourism Impact:** Beyond sports, these games significantly boost **tourism** in **Jammu and Kashmir**. The influx of athletes, coaches, and spectators from across the country highlights the region as a safe and premier destination for global **winter tourism**.
 
• **Mascot and Identity:** Recent editions of the games have used the **Snow Leopard** (often referred to as **‘Sheen-e-She’** or **Shan**) as the mascot to raise awareness about Himalayan wildlife conservation and the spirit of resilience in high altitudes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Participation:** The **2025** games saw participation from various **Indian States**, **Union Territories**, and institutional teams like the **Services Sports Control Board (SSCB)** and the **Army Marksmanship Unit**.
 
• **Infrastructure Development:** Under the **Khelo India** scheme, the government has provided financial assistance to upgrade facilities in **Gulmarg**, including specialized grooming machines for snow slopes and safety equipment for athletes.
 
• **Talent Identification:** Top-performing athletes from the **Khelo India Winter Games** are often selected for specialized training camps funded by the **National Sports Development Fund**.
</ul

questions.question: According to GS Krishnan, which of the following sectors are highlighted in the India BioEconomy Report, 2025?

options.text: BioPharma, BioAgri, BioServices, and Robotics Biotech
BioAgri, BioPharma, Renewable Energy, and BioMedical

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**BioPharma, BioIndustrial, BioAgri, and BioServices**__.

__
 
• The **India BioEconomy Report (IBER) 2025**, as highlighted by **GS Krishnan**, the **President** of the **Association of Biotechnology Led Enterprises (ABLE)**, outlines the massive growth potential of India’s biotechnology sector.
 
• The report identifies four major sectors that constitute the backbone of the Indian bioeconomy: **BioPharma**, **BioIndustrial**, **BioAgri**, and **BioServices**.
 
• The **BioPharma** sector remains the largest contributor, driven by India's strengths in **vaccine manufacturing**, **diagnostics**, and **therapeutics**.
 
• **BioIndustrial** applications focus on sustainable solutions, including the production of **bio-fuels**, **industrial enzymes**, and **bio-plastics** to meet environmental goals.
 
• The **BioAgri** segment emphasizes **genetically modified (GM) seeds**, **bio-fertilizers**, and **bio-pesticides** to enhance agricultural yield and food security.
 
• **BioServices** involves **Contract Research Organizations (CROs)** and **Contract Development and Manufacturing Organizations (CDMOs)**, providing clinical trial and research services to global partners.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Economic Targets:** The Indian bioeconomy is projected to reach a valuation of **$150 billion** by **2025** and aims for a long-term goal of **$300 billion** by **2030**.
 
• **Global Standing:** India is currently ranked among the **top 12** biotechnology destinations in the world and holds the **3rd** position in the **Asia-Pacific** region.
 
• **BioPharma Dominance:** Within the bioeconomy, **BioPharma** accounts for nearly **49% to 50%** of the total share, largely due to India's role as the "Pharmacy of the World."
 
• **Startup Ecosystem:** The number of biotech startups in India has grown exponentially, surpassing **6,000** enterprises, supported by government initiatives like **Startup India**.
 
• **Bio-Services Growth:** This sector is growing rapidly as global pharmaceutical companies outsource **R&D** and **clinical trials** to India due to cost-efficiency and a highly skilled workforce.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regulatory Support:** The **Department of Biotechnology (DBT)** and the **Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC)** are instrumental in providing funding and infrastructure to the industry.
 
• **Bio-IT and Data:** While not a primary pillar like the four mentioned, **Bio-IT** and **Bioinformatics** are emerging as critical enablers for drug discovery and personalized medicine.
 
• **Sustainability:** The **BioIndustrial** sector is aligned with India’s **Net Zero** targets, specifically through the **Ethanol Blending Programme** and the development of **Second-Generation (2G) Bio-refineries**.
 
• **Geographic Hubs:** Major biotechnology clusters have been established in **Bengaluru**, **Hyderabad**, **Pune**, and the **National Capital Region (NCR)** to foster innovation.
 
• **Yearly Performance:** In the year **2023**, the bioeconomy was valued at approximately **$137 billion**, showing a robust year-on-year growth exceeding **10%**.
